objects.name: Step animations
objects.description:
One pair of shapes for each way a step can travel, named for the animation they play.

Each animation has a flow of its own with a single step to click through: Send, Call, Event, Callback, Flash, Bolt drop,
Send with a word, Fail, Timeout, Lost, Rejected, Intercepted (twice: by a shape and by a name), Duplicated, Delayed and Share
(Flash has two, because the step before sets it off).

**Every step animation** plays them all: press **P** to watch them one after the other.

objects.name: Flow structure
objects.description:
One set of shapes for each way steps can be grouped: **Repeat**, **Branch**, **Parallel** and **Flow link**.

Each has a flow of the same name, with the chip, lane tabs and progress bar that go with it.

objects.name: Performance
objects.description:
One shape for each thing a load test can show, named for what it shows.

Open the Performance tab (**T**), pick **Every load effect**, then press **Ramp** or step the levels with the arrow keys.

objects.name: Shape states
objects.description:
One shape that goes through every state, and one that holds another shape in a state.

Play **Every state** to watch a shape start, run, degrade, stop, restart and run again, and **State inside a shape** to see a shape show that something inside it is not running.

objects.name: Runs over time
objects.description:
A run measured over time instead of over load, with events on its timeline that set the state of a shape.

Open the Performance tab (**T**), pick **Every state over time**, then press **Play**, drag the slider or click an event.

objects.name: Send · from
objects.description: `animation: send`. Something runs one way along the line. The sender does not wait.

objects.name: Send · to
objects.description: Takes the envelope in with a squash.

objects.name: Effects · from
objects.description: `animation: { kind: send, effect: bounce }`. What the moving label does on its way, besides travelling. None of them bends its shape.

objects.name: Effects · to
objects.description: Sits down the slope from its sender, so the label runs along a slanted line and shows it stays level.

objects.name: Call · from
objects.description: `animation: call`. The envelope goes, the sender waits, and the reply comes back.

objects.name: Call · to
objects.description: Takes the envelope in, then answers.

objects.name: Event · from
objects.description: `animation: event`. A bolt runs along the line, and the receiver flashes.

objects.name: Event · to
objects.description: Flashes when the bolt arrives.

objects.name: Callback · from
objects.description: `animation: callback`. A ring leaves this shape and a bell runs to the subscriber.

objects.name: Callback · to
objects.description: The subscriber. A ring goes out when the bell arrives.

objects.name: Flash · source
objects.description: Hands something to the publisher, which is what sets the callback off.

objects.name: Flash · from
objects.description: `animation: {kind: callback, trigger: outside}`, right after a step that landed here. This shape flashes, then the bell runs.

objects.name: Flash · to
objects.description: The subscriber.

objects.name: Bolt drop · from
objects.description: `animation: {kind: callback, trigger: outside}`, with no step before it that landed here. A bolt drops onto this shape, then the bell runs.

objects.name: Bolt drop · to
objects.description: The subscriber.

objects.name: Fail · from
objects.description: `animation: {kind: send, outcome: fail}`. The envelope runs to the receiver, which refuses it.

objects.name: Fail · to
objects.description: Flashes when the refusal arrives.

objects.name: Timeout · from
objects.description: `animation: {kind: call, outcome: timeout}`. The envelope goes, the sender waits, no reply comes, and the line dims.

objects.name: Timeout · to
objects.description: Takes the envelope in and never answers.

objects.name: Lost · from
objects.description: `animation: {kind: send, outcome: lost, reason: Packet dropped}`. The envelope runs part of the way, pops, and leaves a cross where it went.

objects.name: Lost · to
objects.description: Never hears of it, so it never squashes or flashes.

objects.name: Rejected · from
objects.description: `animation: {kind: call, outcome: rejected, reason: Rate limit}`. The envelope stops at the bar by the receiver and comes back red.

objects.name: Rejected · to
objects.description: Turns the call away at the door. The bar flashes.

objects.name: Intercepted · from
objects.description: `animation: {kind: call, outcome: intercepted, by: intercepted-by}`. The envelope leaves the line for a third shape, which takes it and lights.

objects.name: Intercepted · to
objects.description: Never gets the call.

objects.name: Intercepted · taken by
objects.tech: not an end of the step
objects.description: The third shape. It gets a dashed outline for the whole step and lights when the envelope arrives.

objects.name: Intercepted by a name · from
objects.description: `animation: {kind: call, outcome: intercepted, by: {name: Café wifi proxy}}`. The party is not in the model, so a dashed marker with its name hangs below the line.

objects.name: Intercepted by a name · to
objects.description: Never gets the call.

objects.name: Duplicated · from
objects.description: `animation: {kind: send, outcome: duplicated, reason: Retried}`. A second copy leaves the first part of the way along and arrives later.

objects.name: Duplicated · to
objects.description: Takes the envelope in twice, with a squash each time.

objects.name: Delayed · from
objects.description: `animation: {kind: call, outcome: delayed, reason: Cold start}`. The envelope waits partway beside a turning dashed clock, then goes on.

objects.name: Delayed · to
objects.description: Takes the envelope in late, then answers.

objects.name: Share of requests · from
objects.description: `animation: {kind: send, outcome: lost, share: 30, at: 0.7}`. Ten requests go one after another and three of them are lost 70 percent of the way along: r1, r2 and r3, each with its own colour and a ring.

objects.name: Share of requests · to
objects.description: Takes in the seven that arrive.

objects.name: Repeat · from
objects.description: The caller. It asks again until the service answers.

objects.name: Repeat · to
objects.description: The service. It is busy on the first two tries.

objects.name: Branch · from
objects.description: Decides which lane happens.

objects.name: Branch · lane A
objects.description: Takes the first lane.

objects.name: Branch · lane B
objects.description: Takes the second lane.

objects.name: Parallel · from
objects.description: Starts all three lanes together.

objects.name: Parallel · lane A
objects.description: Has two steps, so lane A keeps going after the others have finished.

objects.name: Parallel · lane B
objects.description: One step.

objects.name: Parallel · lane C
objects.description: One step.

objects.name: Flow link · from
objects.description: Hands the story to another flow.

objects.name: Flow link · to
objects.description: Where the other flow carries on.

objects.name: Load
objects.description: Where the load comes in. Every shape below is reached from here.

objects.name: Traffic
objects.description: The line from Load gets thicker and busier as the load goes up. The shape itself stays plain.

objects.name: Latency
objects.description: The dots on the line from Load slow down as calls take longer. The shape itself stays plain.

objects.name: Failing calls
objects.description: More and more of the dots on the line from Load turn red. The shape itself stays plain.

objects.name: Strain
objects.description: Busy. The outline runs from green to red as the shape uses more of its capacity, from 10% at 10 requests/s to 100% at 160.

objects.name: Failing shape
objects.description: Busy because calls fail. Failing 5% counts as full, so the outline runs to red early.

objects.name: Queue
objects.description: Waiting. The number is how many calls are waiting, from 0 to 3000. The outline stays plain because only the waiting was measured.

objects.name: Not measured
objects.description: Nothing was measured here, so it stays plain at every load. Missing is never drawn as zero.

objects.name: Rolled up
objects.description:
A shape that holds others shows the worst strain inside it and the waiting added up.

Double-click it to see each part.

objects.name: Rolled up · A
objects.description: Busy and waiting both grow. At 10 requests/s it is 20% busy with nothing waiting, and at 160 it is 90% busy with 120 waiting.

objects.name: Rolled up · B
objects.description: Waits for 10 calls at every load, and gets less busy as the load goes up, from 50% to 30%.

objects.name: State · caller
objects.description: Calls the other shapes. It is always running.

objects.name: State · service
objects.description: Goes through every state, one step at a time.

objects.name: State · holder
objects.description: Holds a part. Shows a ring with a dashed edge while the part is in a state and it has none of its own.

objects.name: State · part
objects.description: The part. Its state shows on the holder at the overview.

objects.name: Time · caller
objects.description: Calls the other shapes. It is always running, and gets busy while the service is off.

objects.name: Time · service
objects.description: Goes through every state as the run plays, one event at a time.

objects.name: Time · holder
objects.description: Holds a part. Shows a ring with a dashed edge while the part is in a state and it has none of its own.

objects.name: Time · part
objects.description: The part. It stops at 45 s and runs again at 72 s, and its state shows on the holder at the overview.

objects.name: Colour and scale
objects.description:
One shape for each thing a run's **source** sets: the colour of the dots, how many dots stand for the calls, and how big each is.

Open the Performance tab (**T**), pick **Colour and scale**, then press **Ramp** or step the levels with the arrow keys.

objects.name: Source
objects.description: Where the calls come in. Every dot on the lines from here is blue, because the run sets a colour.

objects.name: Few calls
objects.description: One dot for every 50 calls a second. The line goes from 50 calls a second to 800, so from 1 dot to 16.

objects.name: Ten times the calls
objects.description: Ten times the calls of Few calls, so ten times the dots, until the screen limit. Past 24 dots at once the line is scaled down, and the key and its numbers say so.

objects.name: Same calls, slower
objects.description: The same calls as Few calls, so the same number of dots, but each call takes longer, so the dots move slower.

objects.name: Bigger calls
objects.description: The more bytes a call carries, the bigger its dot. The area of a dot follows the size of a call, so 1,600 bytes is a dot twice as wide as 400 bytes.

objects.name: Lost calls
objects.description: A share of the calls dies on the way. Each ends in a small pop where it is lost.

objects.name: Rejected calls
objects.description: A share of the calls is turned away at the end of the line. Each stops at a bar and comes back red.

objects.name: Several sources
objects.description:
Two sources of requests at once, each with its own slider, colour and scale: added from separate runs (**Several sources added**) and tested together (**Several sources tested together**).

Open the Performance tab (**T**), pick one of them, then move a slider or press **Ramp** on a source. The chart follows the source you moved last.

objects.name: Source A
objects.description: Where Source A's calls come in. Its dots are blue, one for every 50 calls a second, and bigger than Source B's because its calls carry more.

objects.name: Source B
objects.description: Where Source B's calls come in. Its dots are green, one for every 10 calls a second.

objects.name: Where they meet
objects.description: Both sources send their calls through here. The line to Shared service carries both, so it has a stream of dots for each, side by side, in its colour. Past 24 dots at once both are scaled down together, so the ratio stays true.

objects.name: Shared service
objects.description: Both sources fill it. In the run added from separate runs its use is the two added, and past 100% it reads "Added use is over 100%". In the run tested together it is what was measured with both at once.

objects.name: Not split by source
objects.description: The run says how many calls this line carries but not which source sent them, so its dots are grey and the key says "Other calls".
